label: Bible Study
prompt: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I _____ him? till seven times?
verse: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?
note: Peter thought seven times was generous — Jesus answered with seventy times seven.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the _____, O LORD, and thou art exalted as head above all.
verse: Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and thou art exalted as head above all.
note: David's great prayer of praise: thine is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, the majesty — and the kingdom.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Behold, we put _____ in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
verse: Behold, we put bits in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
note: James' tongue lesson: a small bit steers a whole horse — and a small tongue steers a whole life.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And he shall _____ the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
verse: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
note: The final verse of the Old Testament promises Elijah will come to turn hearts — Luke 1:17 applies it to John the Baptist.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: For he _____ the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.
verse: For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.
note: God 'satisfieth the longing soul' — then Psalm 107 tells rescue stories of wanderers, prisoners, the sick, and storm-tossed sailors.
